title: north-summit-payments-prospect-scratchbook
content:
Goal: quick qual & find an intro into North Summit’s product partnerships org. Thinking pilot for embedding Redwood Inference (hosted or dedicated) into their payouts reconciliation UX (reduce support volume, faster dispute triage).

Top-level thesis: North Summit is mid-market payments processor focused on verticalized merchants (retail + hospitality). They prize latency/SLAs for reconciliation flows and have been touting customer self-service. Good fit for Redwood because: predictable token volumes (batch reconciliation + async chat for support), needs for private deployment to meet contracts with larger hotel chains, and cost pressure on per-transaction compute.

Quick facts harvested: (public + LinkedIn + investor decks)
- HQ: Denver, Series B (2023), ~220 employees
- CTO: Leah Park (ex-FastPay infra lead)
- Head of Partnerships: Omar Suleiman (LinkedIn: OmarS-Summit)
- Core product: transaction processing + merchant dashboard + dispute workflow toolkit
- Recent: announced "Summit Assist" (bot feature) in Q4 2024 — appears rule-based today

Why now (trigger signals):
- Growing merchant churn complaints about dispute turnaround times (public forum threads + G2 reviews)
- New enterprise hotel chain pilot listed in press release — likely need for private deployment / auditability
- Hiring for ML infra on jobs board ("data infra engineer") — suggests internal readiness to work on integrations

Key stakeholders (map + notes):
- Omar Suleiman — Head of Partnerships (pilot ownership / business terms). Likely initial champion.
- Leah Park — CTO (tech eval; cares about latency, KMS, private deployment).
- Priya Nair — Dir of Product (reconciliation & ops). Product will own success metrics (MTTR, false positive rate).
- Support Ops lead (unnamed yet) — could be internal sponsor due to cost-savings argument.

Hypotheses to validate on first call:
1) Volume/shape: daily reconciliation jobs (batch sizes, token distribution) and interactive support ticketing volume for the merchant verticals.
2) Security: do they require customer-managed keys / on-prem data plane for enterprise hotel customers?
3) Decision criteria: cost per ticket, latency SLOs, ability to rollback / A/B rollout.
4) Success metrics: percent reduction in manual triage time, ticket handling time, customer NPS lift for disputes.

Initial outreach play (cold sequence) — 5-step multichannel with personalization hooks:
- Touch 0 (LinkedIn): quick like + comment on their "Summit Assist" post (within 24h). Keep public.
- Touch 1 (Email to Omar): Subject: "Small pilot idea for Summit Assist — reduce dispute triage time by 40%"
  Body quick draft: "Omar — saw Summit Assist — congrats. We helped a payments provider cut manual dispute triage by ~35% using a small inference layer + reconciliation cache. No infra migration for one pilot hotel chain; private deployment available if needed. Quick 15-min to explore?"
- Touch 2 (Voicemail): 2 days after email — short: name, 15-min ask, reference email.
- Touch 3 (Email to Leah if Omar no response): Subject: "Low-friction inference pilot for Summit Assist — private deployment option" — highlight latency SLOs + KMS.
- Touch 4 (Outbound SDR LinkedIn message to Omar + follow-up threads).

Objection handling cheat sheet (short bullets):
- "We already have a rules-based assistant": Redwood can augment, not replace; seed with rules then add inference for fuzzy matches and extraction. Show before/after metrics from pilot.
- "Security / data residency": We offer private deployments with customer-managed KMS and audit logs; we can run inside their VPC or in our dedicated nodes with contract terms.
- "Cost concerns": Start with targeted pilot on high-volume dispute classes; use prefix KV caching and batching to minimize per-ticket tokens. Show modeled cost per ticket.
- "We build this in-house": offer to co-build + knowledge transfer; cost comparison vs 6–9 months of eng work + infra maintenance.

Risk checklist (what would kill the deal):
- They insist on on-prem air-gapped deployment and we cannot meet timeline.
- No clear product owner (partnership org say no capacity).
- Legal/regulatory blockers for extracting transaction-level data to hosted environments.

Competitive watch:
- Large LLM API vendors (L1) — likely easiest for them to spin up but higher cost and less observability.
- Niche inference vendors offering rule+LLM combos — check references (Competitor A: "DisputeIQ" — pitched to hotels in 2024).

Pilot proposal sketch (for internal use / pitch):
- Scope: 6-week pilot, single hotel client subset, integration: batch reconciliation + ticket triage chat endpoint.
- Success criteria: 30% reduction in manual triage time on target dispute types; <200ms median inference latency for triage endpoint; cost per ticket < $0.xx (TBD after token estimate).
- Resources required (both sides): 2 SWEs (Redwood) for integration, 1 solutions engineer for prompt/quality tuning, access to sample dispute logs (anonymized), acceptance of test metric collection.
- Deployment options: Hosted API (fastest) OR Dedicated nodes in their VPC (preferred for enterprise customers).

Playbook next actions (my personal TODOs):
- 1) Build concise one-pager for Omar (customize to Summit Assist language) — target: 1 page + metrics + pilot ask. Owner: Maya. Due: 2025-03-06.
- 2) Pull 3 anonymized dispute examples from Redwood demos that match hotel merchant patterns. Owner: Diego. Due: 2025-03-05.
- 3) Draft quick cost model (tokens per ticket estimate) — Rowan. Due: 2025-03-07.
- 4) Send Touch 1 email to Omar (finalize language with Rowan) — Maya. Schedule: 2025-03-06 morning.

Notes to self / voice memo fragments:
- Keep outreach very outcome-focused. Hotels care about time-to-refund and guest experience.
- Use "private deployment" as a leverage word for enterprise prospects; they respond to words like SLA, KMS, audit trail.
- If Omar pushes back on business case, escalate to Leah with a narrow technical ask (e.g., how would you feel about a 6-week POC running in a dedicated VPC?).

Conversation snippets to try (short):
- "Imagine reducing manual triage by 30% in six weeks with no model training required on your side — just a data pipeline and a validation loop."
- "We can run a canary on 5% of tickets and auto-fail to the current flow if confidence < threshold — low risk for ops."

Metrics to capture during pilot (for dashboard):
- # tickets processed by inference vs baseline
- Median inference latency (ms)
- % reduction in manual touch time (min per ticket)
- Escalation rate and false-positive extraction rate

Potential ask for first intro call (15 min):
- 5 min: context + short case study
- 5 min: understand data shape + security constraints
- 5 min: agree next steps (pilot scope owner + timeline)

End notes: draft one-pager and email this week. Keep thread light. If radio-silence for 2 weeks, try warm intro from mutual connection (Leah -> Omar chain on LinkedIn shows 2 mutuals in infra — check with Rowan).

-- scratchbook end --
